notes: GovDeals returned HTTP 403 (bot-blocked) and the PublicSurplus search page is JS-rendered, so no listings could be read. BidSpotter and Federal Equipment were not tested. Web search found no NovaSeq 6000 lots from state universities, hospitals or agencies in 2025-26. It found only dealer and bankruptcy-liquidation listings, mostly EquipNet and UK dealers, which the earlier S654 probe already covered. No sold or hammer prices from 2026 are visible. The dealer asking prices below are the only price data, and I read them only from search snippets. They suggest a very low resale floor for used 6000s (about $5K to $20K, versus roughly $1M new), but they are not dated 2025-26 or tied to clinical sellers, so they are not usable as a decommission-pace signal.
how_to_mine: This is not a cheap source to mine. It needs a real browser session or a scraper. Run the GovDeals search for 'novaseq' and 'illumina sequencer' and tick the closed/completed-auctions filter. Run PublicSurplus keyword searches for 'sequencer' and 'illumina'. Search BidSpotter and fedequip.com for 'NovaSeq'. Record seller, date, price and bid count. Also check ssllc.com closed auctions, where bankrupt biotechs (not public institutions) sell NovaSeq 6000s, and count lots by quarter.
